name: Arcturus Defense Solutions ARC-EM12 'Scatterstorm'
description:
The Arcturus Defense Solutions ARC-EM12 is an electromagnetic scatter gun that uses a linear electromagnetic accelerator to propel ferromagnetic flechette clusters at velocities exceeding conventional shotshell performance by a factor of three. The weapon has no barrel in the conventional sense — the acceleration coils form a rectangular channel that shapes the flechette spread pattern electromagnetically during launch, allowing the operator to adjust spread width from tight cluster to wide scatter through a dial on the receiver.

The Scatterstorm fundamentally reimagines the shotgun concept. Instead of relying on explosive propellant to push lead pellets through a fixed choke, the ARC-EM12 uses electromagnetic force to launch steel flechettes through a variable-geometry field. The result is a weapon whose pattern can be adjusted in real time — a tight cluster that punches through body armor at 50 meters, or a wide scatter that covers a doorway at five meters. No conventional shotgun can do both.

The weapon draws power from a rechargeable capacitor bank housed in the stock, which provides twenty shots per charge. The charging cycle between shots takes 0.8 seconds — slower than a conventional semi-automatic but fast enough for deliberate aimed fire. The electromagnetic launch produces no muzzle flash, minimal thermal signature, and a distinctive crackling sound rather than a conventional gunshot report.
specifications:
caliber: Ferromagnetic flechettes (equivalent to 12 gauge)
effective_range: 60 meters (tight), 15 meters (wide scatter)
rate_of_fire: 0.8 seconds between shots
magazine_capacity: 20 shots per charge
weight: 4.5 kg
flechette_velocity: 900 m/s
tactical_use: An electromagnetic scatter weapon offering variable-pattern capability unavailable in conventional shotguns. The adjustable spread allows a single weapon to serve as both a precision flechette projector and a wide-pattern area weapon. The high flechette velocity defeats body armor that stops conventional buckshot. The lack of muzzle flash and reduced sound signature provide tactical advantages in low-light and noise-sensitive operations. The 0.8-second charge cycle limits rate of fire compared to conventional semi-automatics.
cultural_context: The Scatterstorm is technology from the future deployed in the present. Most of GLMZ's population doesn't know it exists, and those who do tend to work in fields where knowing is a professional requirement. The weapon represents the bleeding edge of electromagnetic weapons technology applied to a traditionally low-tech weapon class, and its existence raises questions about what else Arcturus is building that hasn't been revealed yet.
story_hooks: A Scatterstorm is used in a public incident, and the flechette wounds baffle every forensic examiner who sees them — the injuries don't match any known weapon. The investigation draws attention that Arcturus desperately wants to avoid.

The electromagnetic scatter field technology is applicable to more than weapons — it could revolutionize manufacturing, materials science, and construction. Someone is trying to steal the technology for its civilian applications, which might actually be more valuable than the weapon.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist electromagnetic scatter gun with an aggressive, angular geometry. The weapon's most striking feature is its open rectangular muzzle assembly—no traditional barrel, just a squared-off electromagnetic aperture with visible coil geometry. The receiver is heavily ribbed and vented to dissipate electromagnetic heat. It reads as purpose-built military hardware: utilitarian, intimidating, devoid of decorative elements.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 94 cm | Receiver width: 8.5 cm | Stock-to-muzzle: 62 cm barrel equivalent | Muzzle aperture: 6 × 4 cm rectangular opening
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced—4.5 kg distributed well across the stock-mounted capacitor assembly. The weight sits rearward, making it shoulder-friendly despite the forward electromagnetic assembly.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced carbon-composite receiver with aerospace-grade aluminum electromagnetic coil housing. Steel reinforcement ribs along the handguard. Polymer-phenolic synthetic stock.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray on the coil housing with visible anodized aluminum striping. The composite receiver is satin black with deliberate weathering—worn edges, micro-abrasions suggesting field use. Heat-scorched polymer around the muzzle aperture.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: matte black and gunmetal gray | Accents: deep blue power indicators along the capacitor assembly, faint copper oxidation on exposed coil edges
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with subtle ribbing for wet-weather handling. The charging mechanism is wrapped in rubberized cable conduit. Handguard features aggressive checkering.
distinctive_features: Open rectangular electromagnetic aperture with visible acceleration coils
Variable-pattern dial on receiver side (mechanical + digital readout)
Capacitor bank spine running along top of stock with status LED strip (blue = charged, amber = charging)
Heat vents positioned in three rows along the receiver sides
Ferromagnetic flechette loader port on upper receiver
Charging cable terminator (magnetic quick-disconnect) mounted on lower stock
No traditional safety—electromagnetic interlock prevents firing with dead capacitors
Muzzle aperture shows heat discoloration from electromagnetic discharge
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Arcturus Defense Solutions logo (interlocking 'A' + stylized star) stamped in gray anodized aluminum on the upper receiver. Serial plate mounted flush on left side. 'IRON POINT AMMUNITION' subsidiary marking on the stock. Warning placards in English and Mandarin on the capacitor assembly.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but meticulously maintained. The polymer shows micro-scratches and scuff marks indicating active use. Coil housing exhibits light heat stress—no rust or corrosion (aluminum construction). The muzzle aperture shows burn marks from repeated electromagnetic discharge. Well-lubricated mechanical components suggest professional upkeep.
